gamespot.com/articles/gta-6s-long-wait-h.excerpt: You might expect people to talk about the visuals, lighting, action sequences, or gunplay after Grand Theft Auto VI's brand-new extended-look trailer showed off over 25 minutes of new footage. But the top comments on Rockstar's YouTube upload of the video deal more with the human condition than expected. In fact, there's quite a bit of talk about death and remembrance. The top comment (at the time of publication) states: "a moment of silence for people that didn't make it here." Meanwhile, another person writes: "Objective: Stay alive till release day." It's been a long wait for GTA 6 , especially since GTA 5 originally launched almost 13 years ago. Not only has a lot happened to the gaming industry as a whole since GTA 5 came out, but also to people's personal lives. For instance, another person typed: "Bro, I went through middle school, high school, and college ... now I need to request time off work for this." Tragedy has apparently struck others, but not dampered their spirits, as seen in this comment: "I was in a traffic accident in February and lost a leg, but I've still got my two damn hands and my eyes, baby!" There is a lot to take in from the new GTA 6 trailer , such as NPCs noticing if you're openly carrying a weapon in the game. In addition, stealing a car might be a little more complicated this time around. For older vehicles, you can still smash the glass, but newer models apparently require a key cloner. GTA 6 is set to finally release on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. It sounds like a playthrough of the open-world game could be roughly 80 hours , so plan accordingly this holiday season.

gamespot.com/articles/fables-loot-is-mea.title: Fable’s Loot Is Meant To Be Meaningful, So Don’t Expect A Bunch Of Minor Upgrades
gamespot.com/articles/fables-loot-is-mea.excerpt: At the heart of many great action-RPGs is a satisfying grind for better loot. Whether it's random chests or quest rewards, it's important to feel like you're getting appropriate payoffs for overcoming challenges. Playground Games, the studio behind the upcoming Fable reboot, told GameSpot it's aiming to make sure that its loot and equipment feels meaningful, with big swings in power level. Creative directors Will Kennedy and Craig Littler told us in an interview at Gamescom that there's lots of variety in the kinds of loot you'll find, and the particularly impactful ones will be new gear. "We want our upgrades to be what we call meaningfully meaningful," Kennedy said. "So you don't get things like, 'Oh, 1% damage,' and things like that. What you get is bigger swings. A good example is the weapon spell we showed. When you first get the weapon spell, you can do a suspend part up in the air. But one of the upgrades you experience is the slam, which really expands the utility and impact of the spell. There's lots of examples like that." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M79EnEkZ-cc With so many options in combat, it's also important to be able to manage your loadouts easily. Kennedy noted that your loadout consists of your melee weapon, ranged weapon, spells, and abilities. Spells and abilities can be upgraded with a skill tree, and then weapons will have their own upgrade path as well. Littler added that the items you find in chests will also play into the game's various systems, including baubles you can give to help your social standing. "You do also find other things in chests," he said. "You might find a gift, for example, that would work with the life system. I don't know what kind of gifts you would find in an old mine, probably a Bag of Blistering or something, but once you've collected that, you can then use that on the NPCs around the world." You can even use sound to draw the enemies out of their hiding spots or toward areas that are more advantageous for you if you're feeling strategic. There are a few varieties of aliens on this planet, but most notable are the giant retro-styled creatures called soldiers, who look like a mash-up between the Predator and the Alien franchise's famous xenomorphs. gamespot.com/articles/saber-boss-reacts-.excerpt: 2026 has been full of big storylines in gaming, including Sony's announcement that it will end support for physical PlayStation game discs in 2028 and the trend of consoles getting increasingly expensive. He said he was "surprised how upset people were" about Sony ending support for physical game discs. Willits said he hasn't bought a physical game "in a long time" because he enjoys the convenience of digital games. Willits is not alone, as the share of digital game sales is growing at numerous companies. At the same time, Sony continues to sell millions of physical game discs annually . Willits said Saber still makes "a lot of money" from physical games, especially in Europe, but the trends are different in North America, he observed. Willits went on to say he had an interaction with someone recently who asked him to sign a copy of Doom 3, a game he worked on when he was with id Software. "So for me personally, I'll miss that in the future," he said. An AI game box? Part of what many people enjoy about physical games is collecting the boxes they come in and presenting them on their shelves. Willits said he thinks someone in the future might create some kind of "AI box" into which players can "upload all your games." "So maybe someone will do that," he said. gamespot.com/articles/saber-responds-to-.excerpt: One of the biggest talking points in gaming today is the use of artificial intelligence, including generative AI. It's a hot-button issue, and few companies have faced the level of criticism about it as Saber has. The developer recently found itself in hot water after CEO Matthew Karch lashed out at Rideshare Stimulator's former writer who said they were laid off and replaced by ChatGPT. Now, Saber's chief creative officer, Tim Willits, has addressed the situation as well, promising that, "We will never fire someone and replace them with AI." For anyone just catching up, Rideshare Stimulator is an upcoming Saber game where players take on the role of an Uber- or Lyft-like driver and interact with them as they take them to their location. The developers freely admit to using generative AI in various capacities, and now Willits has shed more light on the situation. He said the game's main campaign features dialogue written by humans, but there is also a "free ride" mode where Rideshare Stimulator wants to be able to reference current events in the real world. "We use AI to generate that because we want to do it so fast," Willits said, adding that the plan is for weekly or biweekly updates with this kind of AI-generated content. Willits also clarified that some of Saber's other games, including the new Hellraiser, Turok, Stuntman, and Space Marine games, also do not use AI. Saber, like many other game companies, is experimenting with AI in various ways. "We want to figure this new technology out, and we don't know exactly where it's gonna go, and our players don't know where it's gonna go, so we're all ... all of us are trying as a society to figure this out together," he said. "We want to experiment with it. I personally believe somebody [at] some game company will come up with such a brilliant idea, and we'll all be like, 'That's it.' We just need to get there."
